paragraph: Fair Lawn's single-family market is doing the heavy lifting, with 120 sales over six months at a median of $742,500, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.036, and a median of under 20 days on market. Roughly 64 percent of homes sold above asking. That is a real seller's market, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a four-bedroom cape or colonial with two full baths, which is what keeps the median where it is rather than up near the $1,500,000 top of the range. Monthly closings have climbed steadily from 19 in February to 29 in July, right in line with the normal summer peak, and the median has held in the $740,000 to $770,000 band since May after an April spike. If Fair Lawn follows the usual arc, expect volume to taper modestly through fall and stay thin in deep winter. Condos and townhouses are a much smaller slice at 12 sales, and the range runs from $250,000 to $1,050,000, so the $332,500 median is the number to anchor on. Most of what trades there is one-bedroom, one-bath, with a handful of townhouses at far higher prices. If you're weighing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, and in Fair Lawn the condo option is limited enough that you may wait for the right unit.
